_README: HAND-EDITED. calls_score.py reads this file and never writes it.
A ledger of dated market calls from a daily newsletter, graded against
prices after the fact. The point is to learn which KINDS of call carry
information and which are noise, so each call is tagged with a category
and, where one was stated, the author's own confidence.
Enter each call ONCE, on the day it first appears. Newsletters carry old
lines forward for days; re-entering them would count one opinion several
times. When a target is restated at a different number, enter the new one
with `supersedes` pointing at the old id -- that is how drift is tracked.
Paraphrase. Never paste the source text: this repository is public.
FIELDS
id         unique, e.g. 2026-11-24-qqq-hold-630
made       date the call was published (the window opens that session)
by         last session the call covers (inclusive)
ticker     what it is about ('-' for market-wide manual calls)
test       hold   : every session in the window stays at/above level
reach  : some session in the window gets to/above level
under  : every session in the window stays below level
up     : close on `by` above the prior session's close
down   : close on `by` below the prior session's close
manual : not price-testable; graded by hand in `grade`
level      the number, for hold/reach/under
basis      'close' or 'intraday' -- which grade is the headline. Both
are always computed and shown; this only picks the headline.
category   level | target | regime | risk | ticker | conditional | macro
conf       the author's stated probability, 0-1, or null if none given
say        a short neutral paraphrase of the call
supersedes id of an earlier call this one restates at a new number
grade      manual calls only: hit | miss | partial | pending
note       evidence for a manual grade, or context
